elements.element: Customer (Licensee) has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to Licensor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall refund to Customer any prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of such termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term
elements.evidence: Original grants Licensor only breach-based termination: "Upon any breach by Licensee ... the Licensor may immediately terminate"; no convenience right is created, so the condition is demonstrably absent
"upon 30 days' prior written notice" (shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window; preferred level applies)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; instead "Licensor shall refund to Customer any prepaid fees"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: No Licensor convenience-termination right exists or is added; fallback mechanic is absent rather than satisfied

reasons: All atomic elements of the locked preferred level are met: a Customer (Licensee) convenience right, a 30-day written notice period, and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period.

The 'Vendor has no convenience right' element is satisfied by absence: Article IV leaves Licensor with only its existing breach-based immediate termination right, and the insertion creates no Licensor convenience right.

Minimality holds: the drafter added a single concise clause where none existed and did not rewrite Article IV, the 36-month Initial Period, the renewal option, the breach termination right, or the extension mechanics. The short alias sentence ('Licensee is the "Customer" for purposes of this clause IV') is a bridging definition tying the playbook term to the document's party label and introduces no undefined term or contradiction.

Intent preserved: all untouched commercial terms (payment retention on breach, 45-day extension, mutual written extensions) remain effective; no dangling mechanic is created because the refund obligation is self-contained.

Fallback is not independently satisfied (30-day notice sits below the 60–90 day window and no early-termination fee mechanic exists), but that is irrelevant since the preferred bargain is complete and no pieces are combined across levels.
